boundary: Pass 5944 is EXHAUSTIVE over all 3240 covered triples, not sampled. Pass 5946 characterises the odd-q determinant geometry completely at q=3 only. Novelty is not claimed: the line/plane dichotomy in PG(3,3) and the identification of Q+(3,3) with a 4x4 grid are both textbook

pass_5944_the_split_is_projective_span.equivalences: heptad-count 16 <=> perp-size 4 <=> span-rank 2, and all three agree on every triple
pass_5944_the_split_is_projective_span.so: the heptad design's 2-regularity fails at the triple level exactly along the line/plane dichotomy of the ambient projective space, not along anything intrinsic to the symplectic structure
pass_5944_the_split_is_projective_span.the_invariant: whether the three points lie on a PROJECTIVE LINE of PG(3,3). They are pairwise non-collinear in W(3,3) -- no totally isotropic line joins them -- but three of them can still span only a 2-space, a hyperbolic line. Those lie in 16 heptads; triples spanning a plane lie in 33

pass_5946_the_odd_q_analogue.construction: det polarization on M_2(F_3), modulo scalars {+-1}
pass_5946_the_odd_q_analogue.significance: the odd-q determinant construction is not a failure, it is a DIFFERENT geometry. Where char 2 gives the doily W(3,2) with 9+6, char 3 gives the hyperbolic quadric with 16+24. Their #4 next step should target Q+(3,3) at odd q rather than a symplectic lift that Pass 5936 proved cannot exist

the_quadric.reading: Q+(3,3) is the 4x4 grid; polarization-orthogonality is 6-regular on its 16 points and its maximum coclique is 4, a transversal -- the quadric's own ovoid

two_exhaustive_facts: the q=3 heptad design fails at triples exactly on projective span rank 2 vs 3
the odd-q determinant geometry is Q+(3,3) = 16 points + 24 units, max coclique 4
what_is_still_open: whether Sp(4,3) has exactly two orbits on occurring triples
